title: Demonstrate a basic understanding of the horticultural industry

lessons.title: What horticulture is
lessons.html:
What horticulture is

Horticulture is the growing of plants in gardens, nurseries and small intensive farms. It is different from big field crops like maize and wheat. In horticulture we grow plants close together and give each one a lot of care.

Parts of the horticulture industry

  • Production nurseries: grow plants from seed and cuttings. They sell seedlings, shrubs and trees.
  • Retail garden centres: sell plants, pots, compost and tools to the public.
  • Landscaping: design and build gardens for homes, offices, schools, estates and parks.
  • Garden maintenance: look after gardens by mowing, pruning, weeding and watering.
  • Parks and municipalities: look after public parks, sports fields and road verges.
  • Cut flowers: grow roses, proteas and other flowers to sell.
  • Vegetables and fruit: also part of horticulture, for example in tunnels.

Plants we work with

Ornamental plants are plants grown because they look nice. Examples are roses, agapanthus, strelitzia (crane flower), aloes, lavender, lawn grass and many trees and shrubs. South Africa has many beautiful indigenous plants. Many are used in gardens all over the world.

Why horticulture is important

  • It gives jobs to many people, in towns and on farms.
  • Gardens and parks make places beautiful and healthy.
  • Trees give shade and clean the air.
  • Good plants and lawns stop soil from washing away.
  • Waterwise gardens help save water.

South Africa often has dry years and water limits in towns. That is why many clients now ask for gardens with indigenous and waterwise plants, mulch and drip irrigation. When you work in horticulture you help people enjoy plants while using less water.

lessons.title: Working in horticulture
lessons.html:
Working in horticulture

There are many jobs in horticulture. You can start as a general worker and learn more skills over time.

Jobs

JobWhat they do
Nursery workerSows seed, pricks out, pots plants, waters
Garden workerMows, weeds, prunes, plants, waters
Irrigation workerPuts in and fixes sprinklers and pipes
Team leaderLeads a team and checks the work
LandscaperBuilds new gardens
Nursery or garden managerPlans the work, buys stock, manages staff

Good work habits

  • Be on time. Plants need water at the right time.
  • Look after tools. Clean them and put them back.
  • Follow instructions from your team leader.
  • Ask if you do not understand.
  • Be polite to clients and the public. In a garden centre or at a client's home, you represent the company.
  • Respect the client's property. Close gates, keep pets in, and do not walk on flower beds.

Working safely

  • Wear safety boots, gloves and a hat.
  • Use sunscreen and drink water on hot days.
  • Wear ear and eye protection when you use a mower or brushcutter.
  • Lift heavy pots and bags with your knees, not your back.
  • Never use chemicals unless you are trained and allowed to.
  • Tell your team leader at once if you get hurt.

Learning and growing

You can learn more by doing training courses like this one. Many people who started as garden workers now run their own landscaping businesses.

Key points

  • Horticulture is growing plants with intensive care in nurseries, gardens and parks.
  • It includes nurseries, garden centres, landscaping, maintenance and parks.
  • Ornamental plants are grown for their beauty.
  • Good habits: be on time, care for tools, follow instructions, respect clients.
  • Always work safely and report injuries.
